bank.name: Sentence Correction
bank.subject: English
bank.description: Choose the option that makes the sentence grammatically correct.

options: He go to school every day.
He goes to school every day.
He going to school every day.
He gone to school every day.
questions.explanation: With the third-person singular 'he', the present simple verb takes '-s' (goes).
The auxiliary 'doesn't' is followed by the base form 'like'.
The present perfect requires 'have' + past participle (seen).

options: He is more taller than his brother.
He is taller than his brother.
He is tallest than his brother.
He is most taller than his brother.
questions.explanation: Short adjectives form the comparative with '-er', not 'more'.

options: Neither of the boys were present.
Neither of the boys was present.
Neither of the boys are present.
questions.explanation: With 'neither of', the singular verb 'was' is correct.

options: Each of the students have a book.
Each of the students has a book.
Each of the students are having a book.
questions.explanation: 'Each' takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

options: If I was rich, I would travel.
If I were rich, I would travel.
If I am rich, I would travel.
If I be rich, I would travel.
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses 'were' (subjunctive) after 'if'.

options: She is married with a doctor.
She is married to a doctor.
She is married by a doctor.
She is married of a doctor.
questions.explanation: The correct preposition is 'married to'.
'Good at' is used for skills and subjects.

options: I look forward to see you.
I look forward to seeing you.
I look forward to seen you.
questions.explanation: After 'look forward to', the gerund (-ing form) is used.

options: The news have been good today.
questions.explanation: 'News' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb.

options: He has been living here since 2010.
He has been living here since ten years.
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used with a point in time (2010); 'for' is used with a duration.

options: One of my friends are a doctor.
One of my friend is a doctor.
One of my friends is a doctor.
One of my friends were a doctor.
questions.explanation: 'One of + plural noun' takes a singular verb.
The correct structure is 'prefer X to Y'.

options: The committee have decided the matter.
The committee has decided the matter.
The committee are decided the matter.
The committee have been decided the matter.
questions.explanation: Collective nouns such as 'committee' usually take a singular verb.

options: No sooner had he arrived than it started raining.
No sooner he had arrived than it started raining.
No sooner did he arrive when it started raining.
No sooner he arrived than it started raining.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner... than' uses inversion: 'No sooner had he arrived than...'.

options: I am used to wake up early.
I am used to waking up early.
I used to waking up early.
I am use to waking up early.
questions.explanation: 'Be used to' is followed by the gerund (-ing form).

options: This is the girl whom won the prize.
This is the girl who won the prize.
This is the girl which won the prize.
This is the girl whose won the prize.
questions.explanation: 'Who' is the subject relative pronoun for people; 'which' is for things.
Latin-origin comparatives like 'senior' take 'to', not 'than'.

options: She advised me to work hard.
She advised to me to work hard.
She advised that I must work hard.
questions.explanation: The structure is 'advise + object + to-infinitive'.

options: I have less money than him.
I have fewer money than him.
I have lesser money than him.
I have little money than him.
questions.explanation: 'Less' is used with uncountable nouns such as money.

options: The scenery of Murree are beautiful.
The scenery of Murree is beautiful.
The sceneries of Murree is beautiful.
The scenery of Murree were beautiful.
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

options: He has not been to Lahore since a month.
He has not been to Lahore for a month.
He has not been to Lahore from a month.
He has not been to Lahore until a month.
questions.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration of time (a month).

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'One of my friend lives in Lahore.'
options: One of my friend → one of my friends
questions.explanation: After 'one of' the noun must be plural: 'one of my friends'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He insisted to pay the bill.'
questions.explanation: 'Insist' takes the preposition 'on': 'insisted on paying the bill'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The news are good today.'
questions.explanation: 'News' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'The news is good'.
With 'does', the main verb stays in the base form: 'does not like'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'I have visited Karachi last year.'
questions.explanation: 'Last year' is a definite past time, so the simple past is required: 'I visited Karachi last year'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He asked me that where I lived.'
questions.explanation: Wh-questions in reported speech do not need 'that': 'He asked me where I lived'.

options: Scarcely had he arrived when it started raining
Scarcely he had arrived when it started raining
Scarcely had he arrived than it started raining
Scarcely he arrived when it starts raining
questions.explanation: 'Scarcely...when' uses inversion: 'Scarcely had he arrived when...' (never 'than').

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He prefers tea than coffee.'
questions.explanation: 'Prefer' takes 'to': 'He prefers tea to coffee'.

options: She advised me to not go there
She advised me not to go there
She advised me not go there
She advised me to not going there
questions.explanation: The negative infinitive is 'not to go', with 'not' placed before 'to'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The committee are divided in its opinion.'
options: are divided in its opinion → are divided in their opinion
questions.explanation: If 'committee' is treated as plural ('are'), the pronoun must agree: 'are divided in their opinion'.

options: He is the tallest of the two brothers
He is the taller of the two brothers
He is tallest of the two brothers
He is the taller among the two brothers
questions.explanation: For two people use the comparative 'taller', not the superlative 'tallest'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He has not written to me since a month.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' needs a point in time; for a duration use 'for a month'.

options: I look forward to hear from you
I look forward to hearing from you
I look forward for hearing from you
I look forward to heard from you
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' is followed by the gerund: 'to hearing'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He has been sleeping for three hours.'
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: present perfect continuous with a duration ('for three hours').

options: If I was you, I would accept
If I were you, I would accept
If I am you, I would accept
If I be you, I would accept
questions.explanation: The subjunctive 'were' is used in the second conditional: 'If I were you'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The sceneries of Murree are beautiful.'
questions.explanation: 'Scenery' is uncountable and has no plural form.

options: He denied to take the money
He denied to took the money
questions.explanation: 'Deny' takes a gerund: 'denied taking'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'I have bought this car for five years.'
questions.explanation: 'Buy' is momentary; with a duration use 'have had' (state verb).

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Let's discuss about the plan.'
questions.explanation: 'Discuss' is transitive and takes no preposition: 'discuss the plan'.

options: He has left for Lahore yesterday
He had left for Lahore yesterday
questions.explanation: 'Yesterday' requires simple past: 'He left for Lahore yesterday'.

options: He suggested to me to go
questions.explanation: 'Suggest' takes a that-clause or gerund, never 'suggest me to'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The furniture are expensive.'
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable and takes a singular verb: 'is expensive'.

options: He is very good in mathematics
He is very good at mathematics
He is very good for mathematics
He is very good with mathematics
questions.explanation: 'Good at' + skill/subject is the correct idiom.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Hardly had he reached the station when the train left.'
questions.explanation: The sentence is correct: 'Hardly...when' with inversion and past perfect.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He asked that why she was late.'
questions.explanation: Wh-word questions in reported speech drop 'that': 'He asked why she was late'.

options: Neither Ali nor his brothers is coming
Neither Ali nor his brothers are coming
Neither Ali nor his brothers was coming
Neither Ali or his brothers are coming
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject (brothers) → 'are'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He told to me that he was tired.'
questions.explanation: 'Tell' takes a direct object: 'told me', not 'told to me'.

options: He has been sleeping since 9 p.m.
questions.explanation: 'Since 9 p.m.' with a continuing action requires present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'I have a little knowledge about the subject.'
questions.explanation: 'Little' (almost none) is negative; 'a little' means some. The intended meaning determines it.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The team were playing well yesterday.'
questions.explanation: Collective nouns may take plural verbs when members act individually — acceptable usage.
The polite order is 'Ali and I'; 'I' is the subject pronoun.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He has gone to London two days ago.'
options: two days ago → two days before
questions.explanation: 'Two days ago' is a definite past time → simple past 'went'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He is more taller than his brother.'
questions.explanation: 'Taller' is already comparative; 'more taller' is a double comparative.
'Good at' + sport/activity is the correct idiom.

options: I am having a lot of work
I have a lot of work
I have been having much work
questions.explanation: 'Have' meaning possession is a state verb, not used in continuous: 'I have a lot of work'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He asked me where did I live.'
options: where did I live → where I lived
questions.explanation: Indirect questions use statement order: 'where I lived'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Each of the boys were given a prize.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular → 'was given'.

options: If I was you, I would go
If I were you, I would go
If I am you, I would go
If I be you, I would go
questions.explanation: Second conditional uses subjunctive 'were': 'If I were you'.

options: He is elder than his brother
He is older than his brother
He is eldest than his brother
He is more elder than his brother
questions.explanation: Compare two people by age → 'older than'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'The teacher asked the students to not make noise.'
options: to not make → not to make
questions.explanation: Negative infinitive: 'not to make'.

options: It has been raining since morning
questions.explanation: Continuing action → present perfect continuous.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He is suffering from fever since Monday.'
questions.explanation: With 'since Monday' and continuing action → present perfect continuous.

options: He asked me where did I live
He asked me where I lived
He asked me where do I live
He asked me that where I lived
questions.explanation: Indirect questions use statement word order.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'Each of the students have submitted the assignment.'
questions.explanation: 'Each' is singular → 'has submitted'.

options: The house that I live in is old
The house that I live is old
The house that I live at is old
The house that I live to is old
questions.explanation: The relative clause 'that I live in' needs the preposition.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He does not likes tea.'
options: does not likes → does not like
questions.explanation: After 'does', the main verb stays in base form: 'does not like'.

options: Neither of the two answers are correct
Neither of the two answers is correct
Neither of the two answers were correct
Neither of the answers are correct
questions.explanation: 'Neither' is singular → 'is correct'.

questions.prompt: Identify the error: 'He told that he is busy.'
questions.explanation: 'Tell' needs an object (told me); without one use 'said'.
The correct idiom is 'married to'.

options: He has been working here since five years
He has been working here for five years
He has been working here from five years
He has been working here at five years
questions.explanation: For is used with a duration of time: for five years.

options: I look forward to meet you
I look forward to meeting you
I look forward to met you
questions.explanation: Look forward to takes a gerund: to meeting.
Prevent takes 'from + gerund'.

options: No sooner did he arrive than it started raining
No sooner he arrived than it started raining
No sooner did he arrive when it started raining
No sooner he arrives than it rains
questions.explanation: No sooner is followed by 'than', with inversion after did.
Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior) take to.

options: He told that he was unwell
He said that he was unwell
He told to me that he was unwell
He said me that he was unwell
questions.explanation: Say takes 'to + person' or nothing; tell requires an object.

options: He is one of the best players who has won the trophy
He is one of the best players who have won the trophy
He is one of the best player who have won the trophy
He is the one of the best players who has won the trophy
questions.explanation: In 'one of + plural noun + who', the verb agrees with the plural antecedent.

options: He insisted on paying the bill
He insisted to pay the bill
He insisted for paying the bill
questions.explanation: Insist is followed by 'on + gerund'.
Prefer X to Y is the correct construction.

options: He is not only intelligent but also hardworking
He is not only intelligent but hardworking also
He is only not intelligent but also hardworking
Not only he is intelligent but also hardworking
questions.explanation: Not only...but also is the correct correlative pair.
News is uncountable and takes a singular verb.

options: She has gone to the market yesterday
She went to the market yesterday
She has went to the market yesterday
She is going to the market yesterday
questions.explanation: A definite past time (yesterday) requires the simple past.
When the committee acts as one body, use a singular verb.

options: I had visited Lahore in 2019 already
I have been visiting Lahore in 2019
questions.explanation: A finished past moment (in 2019) needs the simple past.
Angry with a person is the standard idiom.

options: She has been sleeping for two hours
She has been sleeping since two hours
She slept for two hours now
She has slept for two hours ago
questions.explanation: For + duration is correct with the present perfect continuous.

options: Neither he nor his friends was invited
Neither he nor his friends were invited
Neither he nor his friends is invited
Neither he nor friends was invited
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject (friends → were).

options: I have a lot of work to do today
I have lot of works to do today
I have many works to do today
I have much works to do today
questions.explanation: Work is uncountable; use a lot of, not many/much with plural.

options: She said she will come tomorrow
She said she would come the next day
She said she will come the next day
She says she would come tomorrow
questions.explanation: In reported speech, will becomes would and tomorrow becomes the next day.

options: He works hard so that he may pass
He works hard so that he may passed
He works hard so that he can passed
He works hard so that he might passed
questions.explanation: So that is followed by may/can + base verb.
Elder is used for family members without than; older is the general comparative with than.

options: I have not seen him since Monday
I have not seen him for Monday
I have not seen him from Monday
I have not seen him after Monday
questions.explanation: Since is used with a point in time: since Monday.

options: He is enough strong to lift it
He is strong enough to lift it
He is strong enough lifting it
He is enough strong lifting it
questions.explanation: Enough follows the adjective: strong enough.
Furniture is uncountable and takes a singular verb.
Interested in is the correct idiom.
Discuss takes a direct object without a preposition.

options: She suggested that I should go
She suggested to me to go
questions.explanation: Suggest takes a that-clause, not an indirect object.

options: He returned back the book again
He returned back the book late
questions.explanation: Return already implies back; adding back is redundant.

options: Hardly had I left when the phone rang
Hardly I had left when the phone rang
Hardly had I left than the phone rang
Hardly I left when the phone rang
questions.explanation: Hardly...when with inversion is the correct structure.

options: Each of student has a book
questions.explanation: Each is singular and takes a singular verb.

options: The police has caught the thief
The police have caught the thief
The police is catching the thief
The police has catch the thief
questions.explanation: Police is a collective noun that takes a plural verb.

options: He has less money than his brother
He has fewer money than his brother
He has lesser money than his brother
He has few money than his brother
questions.explanation: Less is used with uncountable nouns like money.
